This year I plan like I always do — I start from what worked last year and adjust a little. My 10.1 mu is split: I keep 6 mu for the wheat-maize rotation because that is my main income, and I give 4.1 mu to cotton. Cotton takes more work but the price has been decent and my husband helps on weekends when he is back from the city.

For my wheat this winter, I will plant Jimai improved seed — the input dealer in town said it holds up well in our soil, and my neighbor Wang had 450 kg last year with it. I use about 2 bags of compound fertilizer as base (that gives me roughly 18 kg N, 9 kg P, 7 kg K per mu), and then I top-dress urea at green-up, maybe 10 kg per mu. I would rather put a bit extra than see yellow leaves in spring. I irrigate 4 times — winter water, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray 2 times, once for aphids and once for the wheat scab if weather is wet.

For summer maize after the wheat, I go with Zhengdan hybrid — everyone around here uses it. I apply about 16 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu, with the urea side-dressed at knee-high. Maize is thirsty but the summer rains help, so I only pump from the well 2 times. One pesticide spray for corn borer is usually enough.

Cotton is different — I give it more potassium because the bolls need it, and more sprays because the bollworm is bad some years. About 14 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K per mu. I irrigate 3 times and spray 4 times — cotton without spraying is no cotton at all.

I plough before cotton because the soil needs loosening, but for wheat and maize I just do rotary tillage — saves diesel money and time.
